title: ZIMSEC O-Level English Language

officialDocument.title: English Language Syllabus, Forms 1 - 4, 2015 - 2022 (Ministry of Primary and Secondary Education, Curriculum Development and Technical Services), examined by ZIMSEC at O Level
officialDocument.publisher: Ministry of Primary and Secondary Education (Curriculum Development and Technical Services) / Zimbabwe School Examinations Council (ZIMSEC)

sourceNote: Section headings and numbers (7.1 to 7.5) and the aspects and sub-topics under them are transcribed from the scope and sequence (7.0) of the Ministry's English Language Syllabus Forms 1 - 4 (2015 - 2022); the competency matrix (8.0) supplied the content of each aspect. Topic and sub-topic codes below the section numbers (7.1.1, 7.3.1.1, ...) and objective codes are ours, not the board's. Learning-objective statements are our own paraphrase; no syllabus text is reproduced.
notes: Source (read 2026-10-08): the Mashonaland West provincial education office's copy of the Ministry document (http://www.mopsemashwest.gov.zw/files/English%20Language%20Syllabus.pdf, linked from its O-Level syllabus page; the site's https certificate has expired), read through a text rendering. The document is dated 2015 and covers Forms 1 to 4. The text rendering of the scope-and-sequence and competency-matrix tables scrambles some cells, so absence of an item is less certain than its presence. Check every heading and objective against a clean copy from ZIMSEC and record the exact document URL.
Subject code: not printed in the syllabus document. ZIMSEC O-Level English Language is commonly cited as 1122; confirm it (code left null).

Version dates: assumed first examined in November 2018 (effectiveFrom 2018-01-01), as for the other 2015-2022 files. Under the Heritage-Based Curriculum (2024-2030) new syllabi were issued; confirm which syllabus the November 2026 and later O-Level English Language examinations use, set effectiveTo, and create a new version file when a new syllabus replaces this one.

Assessment (9.0) as read: continuous assessment 30% (speaking, listening, reading, writing and a project, Forms 1 to 4) and a summative examination 70%: Paper 1 Composition (1 hour 30 minutes; Section A, 30 marks, one composition from seven topics that may be narrative, descriptive, informative, argumentative or discursive; Section B, 20 marks, one compulsory guided composition from notes, text, graphs, statistical data or pictures: a letter, speech, report, article or memorandum) and Paper 2 Comprehension, Summary and Supporting Language Structures (2 hours; Section A, 40 marks, a prose passage with comprehension questions and a summary question; Section B, 10 marks, questions on language structures set in the context of the passage). The assessment model weights compositions 35% and comprehension with language structures 35% of the whole subject, so the components carry no weightingPercent. The split of the 40 Section A marks between comprehension and summary is not stated.
Paper 2 specification grid as read: simple recall 12%, comprehension and application 80%, analysis, synthesis and evaluation 8%.

Listening, speaking and the project are assessed only in continuous assessment. The platform has no audio, so the listening content is limited to strategies and practice from written transcripts; speaking content covers preparation, conventions and pronunciation knowledge.

The document lists the topics (6.2) as oral work, language structures, comprehension, composition, summary and registers; this tree follows the more detailed scope and sequence (skills 1 to 4 and topic 5) instead, with summary under intensive reading and registers under both speaking and writing.

components.name: Paper 1: Composition
components.description: Section A (30 marks): one composition from a choice of seven topics (narrative, descriptive, informative, argumentative or discursive). Section B (20 marks): one compulsory guided composition (letter, speech, report, article or memo) based on notes, text, graphs, statistics or pictures.

components.name: Paper 2: Comprehension, summary and supporting language structures
components.description: Section A (40 marks): comprehension questions and a summary question on a prose passage. Section B (10 marks): language-structure questions set in the context of the passage.

topics.name: Listening and observing
topics.description: Skill 1 in the scope and sequence (Forms 1 to 4): listening comprehension, oral instructions, conversations and purposeful listening.

children.name: Listening comprehension, instructions and messages
children.description: Forms 1 to 4: questions on stories and narrations, note taking, summary, inference and evaluation; directions, announcements, messages, dialogues, interviews, dictation and directed or selective listening.

objectives.text: Listen to stories, broadcasts and narrations and answer recall, inference and evaluation questions on them.
Take notes and summarise what has been heard, and draw a lesson or moral from a story.
Follow a series of spoken directions and instructions and relay messages and announcements accurately.
Take dictation accurately and report back on a talk or presentation.

topics.name: Speaking and signing
topics.description: Skill 2 in the scope and sequence: pronunciation, registers, descriptions, debates and speeches.

children.name: Pronunciation
children.description: Forms 1 to 4: vowels, consonant clusters, diphthongs and triphthongs, silent consonants, weak and strong forms, intonation and stress, tone and mood.

objectives.text: Pronounce English vowel and consonant sounds, diphthongs and words with silent letters accurately.
Use word and sentence stress and rising and falling intonation correctly.
Use tone of voice to express emotion and mood.

children.name: Registers and conversations
children.description: Forms 1 to 4: introductions, greetings, requests, invitations, apologies and compliments, telephone conversations, gratitude, advice, opinions, complaints, condolences, persuasion and interviews; formal and informal situations.

objectives.text: Use polite, appropriate language for greetings, introductions, requests, invitations, apologies, complaints and condolences.
Hold telephone conversations and interviews in formal and informal situations.
Adjust the degree of formality to the listener and the situation.

children.name: Descriptions, debates and speeches
children.description: Forms 1 to 4: describing self, people, scenes, objects, processes and events; debating local, national and international topical issues and cross-cutting themes; prepared and impromptu speeches.

objectives.text: Describe people, scenes, objects, processes and events clearly in speech.
Present opinions on topical issues and argue for or against a motion, arranging ideas logically with discourse markers.
Plan and deliver prepared speeches and give meaningful impromptu speeches.

topics.name: Reading and signing
topics.description: Skill 3 in the scope and sequence: intensive reading, extensive reading and referencing.

children.name: Intensive reading
children.description: Forms 1 to 4: recall and higher-order questions, skimming and scanning, inference, word meaning, note making, summary, synthesis, paraphrasing and evaluation.

children.name: Recall and comprehension questions
children.description: Answering recall and comprehension questions; skimming and scanning; paraphrasing.

objectives.text: Answer recall questions by locating information that a passage states directly.
Skim a text for its general meaning and scan it for specific details.
Paraphrase information from a text in their own words.

children.name: Inference, analysis and evaluation
children.description: Drawing inferences; following the sequence of events and the development of an argument; how language shows the relationships between ideas; main points and supporting detail; bias and stereotyping.

objectives.text: Draw inferences about information that a text does not state directly.
Follow the sequence of events in a narrative and the development of an argument or discussion.
Recognise how words and phrases show the relationships between ideas in a text.
Distinguish main ideas from examples and qualifying details, and recognise bias and stereotyping.

children.name: Contextual meaning of words and phrases

objectives.text: Work out the meanings of words and phrases from the context in which they are used.

children.name: Tone, mood, style and the writer's attitude

objectives.text: Identify the tone and mood of a text and the writer's attitude to the subject.
Comment on the style of a text and the effect of the writer's choice of words and images.
Make brief, relevant notes on texts that have been read.
Select the points in a passage that are relevant to a summary question.
Summarise specific aspects of a text in continuous prose, in their own words and within a word limit.

children.name: Extensive reading
children.description: Forms 1 to 4: summary, characters and characterisation, setting, plot, themes and style of books read.

objectives.text: Read a variety of books for knowledge and enjoyment and summarise them.
Describe and compare major and minor characters and describe the setting of a story.
Identify the plot, the themes and the style of a text and the relationships among its themes.

children.name: Referencing
children.description: Forms 1 to 4: reference sources, sections of a book, encyclopaedias, journals and the internet.

objectives.text: Use reference sources such as dictionaries, encyclopaedias, journals and the internet to find information, observing cyber ethics.
Identify the sections of a book and their purposes.

topics.name: Writing and brailing
topics.description: Skill 4 in the scope and sequence: aspects of composition writing, free compositions and guided compositions.

children.name: Aspects of composition writing
children.description: Forms 1 to 4: sentence construction, types of sentences, elements and unity of a paragraph, registers, linking devices and discourse markers, amplification of notes and figurative language.

objectives.text: Write a variety of correct sentence types.
Write unified, coherent paragraphs with a clear introduction, body and conclusion.
Link sentences and paragraphs with appropriate discourse markers.
Use a register suited to the audience, purpose and situation in letters, speeches, reports and other writing.
Recognise figures of speech and use figurative language for effect in their own writing.

children.name: Free compositions
children.description: Forms 1 to 4: narrative, descriptive, informative, argumentative and discursive compositions and creative writing. Examined in Paper 1 Section A.

objectives.text: Write narrative compositions using techniques such as description, detail, pace, atmosphere, tone and mood, and flashback.
Write detailed descriptions of people, places, scenes, events and processes.
Write informative and expository compositions that explain a subject clearly.
Write persuasive and argumentative compositions that argue logically for a point of view.
Write discursive compositions that consider different sides of an issue.

children.name: Guided compositions
children.description: Forms 1 to 4: letters, reports, speeches, memos, articles and curricula vitae; forms; guided composition techniques (register, correct sentences, amplification, format, paragraphing). Examined in Paper 1 Section B.

objectives.text: Write formal and informal letters in the correct format and register.
Write memoranda in the correct format.
Write reports in the correct format and register.
Write speeches for given occasions and audiences.
Write articles for magazines and newspapers.
Compile a curriculum vitae and complete forms following the instructions given.
Amplify notes (pegs) and write from information given as notes, text, graphs, statistical data or pictures.

topics.name: Supporting language structures
topics.description: Topic 5, taught in context from Form 1 to Form 4 across all skills. Examined in Paper 2 Section B in the context of the comprehension passage.

children.name: Nouns
children.description: Types of nouns, plural forms, gender, opposites, noun formation, prefixes and suffixes.

objectives.text: Identify types of nouns and use plural and gender forms correctly.

children.name: Verbs
children.description: Types of tenses, subject-verb agreement, sequence of tenses, auxiliaries and modals, phrasal verbs, active and passive forms.

children.name: Tenses and the sequence of tenses

objectives.text: Form and use the tenses correctly and keep the sequence of tenses consistent, including in conditional sentences.
Make verbs agree with their subjects.
Use auxiliary and modal verbs correctly.
Use phrasal verbs correctly in context.
Change sentences from the active to the passive form and back.

children.name: Pronouns
children.description: Personal, relative, possessive and reflexive pronouns.

objectives.text: Use personal, relative, possessive and reflexive pronouns correctly.

children.name: Adjectives
children.description: Formation, comparatives and superlatives, opposites, prefixes and suffixes, order when more than one follow each other, non-gradable adjectives.

objectives.text: Form adjectives, use comparatives and superlatives, and order several adjectives correctly.

children.name: Adverbs
children.description: Formation; adverbials of manner, time, place and reason; adverbial phrases and clauses.

objectives.text: Form adverbs and use adverbials of manner, time, place and reason, and adverbial phrases and clauses.

children.name: Spelling and word formation
children.description: Consonant-vowel combinations, spelling rules, prefixes and suffixes, derivative words, noun formation, homonyms, homophones and homographs.

objectives.text: Form derivative words with prefixes and suffixes and use the correct word form in a sentence.
Distinguish homonyms, homophones and homographs and use them correctly.
Apply spelling rules and spell commonly used words correctly.
Use synonyms, opposites and idioms appropriate to the subject matter.

children.name: Sentence construction
children.description: Simple, compound and complex sentences; conjunctions, phrases and clauses; punctuation; articles, determiners and prepositions; questions, question tags, commands and exclamations; discourse markers and sentence modifiers.

objectives.text: Construct simple, compound and complex sentences and identify phrases and clauses.

children.name: Conjunctions, discourse markers and sentence modifiers

objectives.text: Join ideas with conjunctions, discourse markers and sentence modifiers.
Use articles and determiners correctly.
Use prepositions correctly.
Punctuate sentences correctly and explain how punctuation affects meaning.

children.name: Questions, question tags, commands and exclamations

objectives.text: Form questions, question tags, commands and exclamations correctly.

children.name: Direct and indirect speech
children.description: Punctuation and switching between direct and indirect speech.

objectives.text: Punctuate direct speech and change direct speech into indirect speech and back.
